subject: pe
title: Applications in Sport
welcome_lead: Time to put physiology into action and see how the body delivers oxygen during exercise.
meta_desc: GCSE PE applications: tidal volume, breathing rate, cardiac output and exercise responses.
final_note: Excellent work — you can now calculate and apply key physiology numbers.

concepts.def: Volume of air inhaled or exhaled in one normal breath.
Number of breaths taken per minute.
Tidal volume × breathing rate (litres per minute).
Volume of blood pumped per heartbeat.
Stroke volume × heart rate (litres per minute).
Movement of gas from high to low concentration.

walkthroughs.body_html: Minute ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate. If tidal volume is 0.5 L and breathing rate is 12 breaths/min, ventilation = 0.5 × 12 = 6 L/min. During exercise both rise, increasing oxygen supply.
Cardiac output (Q) = stroke volume × heart rate. A resting athlete with SV 70 ml and HR 60 bpm has Q = 4200 ml/min = 4.2 L/min. Training increases stroke volume, so resting heart rate drops.

walkthroughs.h2: How the body adapts to a sprint
walkthroughs.body_html: During exercise breathing rate, tidal volume, heart rate and stroke volume all rise. This boosts oxygen delivery and removes carbon dioxide faster. Blood is redirected to working muscles.
